turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
I have a call at 4:40, Hale, so let's not waste it. Owen found out about his zero on his phone, in the middle of a class, and nobody called me first. Who decided that, and on what basis?
Go ahead, Hale. Finish. I'm writing down whatever comes next.
I have 140 students. I don't have time to be cross-examined by every parent with a law degree.
That's not Owen's problem, Hale. You had time to enter a zero; you can find time to tell me who decided it and on what. Otherwise I'm going to the principal's office when I leave here.
You don't get to talk to me like I'm on the stand.
Then stop answering like you're on it. One question, Hale: was Owen heard before that zero went in, yes or no?
